results.quote: Six crucibles, 1 at the charging end, 6 at the tapping end.
Whole units of melt; any split rounds down. (non-negativity not stated)
Working volume: 10, 8, 12, 6, 9, 7
Upper mark: 7, 6, 9, 5, 7, 5
Lower mark: 3, 2, 4, 2, 3, 2
Starting melt: 3, 6, 6, 2, 2, 1 Everything starts BASE.
Line limit for the emergency tap: 38. ... Slag tally: everything that reached the pit.
Five moves per cycle, each finished down the whole line before the next.
Charge. Pour the row in; nobody watches volume while charging.
Walk 1 to 6. Anything over working volume runs down the launder into the next crucible before you judge that one
runs down the launder into the next crucible before you judge that one, so it can chain.
Overflow off 6 goes to the slag pit.
A BASE crucible at or above its upper mark goes SUPERHEATED.
A SUPERHEATED one at or below its lower mark drops back to BASE.
In between, it holds. Log every change.
Bleed. Read all six before touching any.
BASE crucibles skim a quarter to slag.
SUPERHEATED crucibles send half back up the return launder to the crucible before them; crucible 1 has nowhere to send it, so its half goes to slag.
A crucible can finish over volume; that waits for next cycle's overflow, and after cycle 5 it stays.
Emergency tap. Total the line. Strictly over 38
halve every crucible, removed melt to slag, log the cycle.

the melt in crucibles 1 to 6, in order; each crucible's state (BASE or SUPERHEATED); every change as (cycle, crucible, before, after); the cycles in which an emergency tap fired; the slag tally; and a balance line: starting melt plus all charges, against what is in the crucibles plus slag.
